newsitem.title: CHINA: Asia-Pacific c.bank governors to meet in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Asia-Pacific c.bank governors to meet in Shanghai.

text.p: Governors from 11 central banks and monetary authorities in the Asia/Pacific region meeting on Friday in Shanghai will discuss regional economic and monetary issues, the People's Bank of China said on Thursday.
No communique was scheduled from the meeting, an official of China's central bank said.

However, foreign exchange dealers in the region were looking for some signal from the meeting on possible central bank cooperation on foreign exchange intervention in the wake of recent currency turmoil.
It will be the second governors' meeting of the Executive Meeting of East Asia and Pacific (EMEAP), a regional forum set up in 1991, the Chinese central bank official said.

Central bank and monetary authority governors from Australia, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, New Zealand, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand would attend the one-day meeting, he said.
In the morning session, each country would outline its own economic situation, the official said.
In the afternoon, the governors would sum up their work over the last year while three working groups would discuss bank supervision and management, currency policy and financial markets, he said.
The EMEAP has held 13 meetings of deputies and last July held its first governors' meeting in Tokyo.
